# Pinned local history admission patch

Upstream: `yrs` 0.28.0, y-crdt/y-crdt revision `23b7f5693bbf9e7d26340c521ee8647f79bdfba2`, registry archive SHA-256 `52c70dc8beca8666c77612a96889106ca3cd65318609721f464624ff79685da9`. `UPSTREAM.json` records the unmodified registry members and their hashes; only `src/transaction.rs` differs. Upstream MIT license is retained in `LICENSE` from that exact revision. Package source and benches are retained; registry installation markers and the package-local Cargo.lock are omitted.

The only source patch adds `TransactionMut::copy_local_redone_from`. It copies Yrs local redone pointers by CRDT client/clock ranges to a freshly decoded exact checkpoint replica. Wire encoding does not carry these pointers. Without them, copying UndoManager stacks into a disposable replica can restore a second copy of earlier overwritten text rather than following a prior inverse, so admission differs from the eventual live mutation. No alternative undo, semantic, projection or wire owner is introduced.

The target must be a disposable, GC-disabled replica freshly restored from the source's complete checkpoint, with identical retained structs and deletion set. The source stays read-locked during copying; the source may use GC because its UndoManagers retain their tracked deleted items. Snapshot equality and target GC policy are checked before any copy. Target blocks are split to the source clock ranges; copied pointers preserve the offset within each range. Only local metadata changes, without an inserted/deleted item or content event. Never invoke this on a remote/untrusted replica or a live editor.

The owning caller is `Document::history_apply`, before the disposable UndoManager and all existing admission/immutable-structure/selection checks. All source limits, capture scopes, history effects and live publication ordering remain unchanged. See `history_replica.rs` and the full-limit v4/v5 repeated overwrite regression in `history.rs`; the native fixed-Long Session/SQLite scenario is the owning integration proof. Upstream dependency updates must revalidate or retire this patch rather than silently replacing it.
